summary: Remove overly-broad Pattern 3 from answer cleaning to prevent corruption of counting/tracking answers; retain conservative formatting for choice-format answers

edits.hypothesis: Normalize choice-format answers by converting bare choice letters to parenthesized form and removing trailing descriptions from parenthesized choices, using only conservative patterns that match clear choice context.
edits.targets_mode: answer extraction format issues: parenthesized choices with appended descriptive text, and bare choice letters that should be parenthesized
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Post-processing extraction cleanup (regex on extracted ANSWER lines) is control-flow logic, not prompt/reasoning—deterministic normalization requires plumbing changes
edits.trigger_condition: Applied to all ANSWER: lines; Case 1 wraps bare A-F alone in parentheses; Case 2 strips trailing text from (A-F) format; no pattern matches bare letter + description to avoid corrupting non-choice answers
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Format failures like '(D) Rodrigo'→'(D)' and '(B) orange ball'→'(B)' are fixed by Case 2; (preservative) passing clean-answer tasks unaffected since they already have correct format; (transfer) choice normalization generalizes to any multi-choice task family
edits.regression_risk: Removed Pattern 3 (bare A-F + any following text) to prevent false matches on counting/tracking answers like 'B 5'→'(B)'. Retained only Patterns 1 (bare letter alone) and 2 (parenthesized with description), both conservative and task-safe.
edits.mechanism: Normalize choice-format answers by converting bare choice letters to parenthesized form and removing trailing descriptions from parenthesized choices, using only conservative patterns that match clear choice context.

edits.hypothesis: Simplify output by keeping only lines from 1 line before ANSWER: to end, discarding verbose preamble; since grader extracts only ANSWER: line, this reduces confusion without loss.
edits.targets_mode: verbose extracted answers where explanatory preamble causes confusion (linguini family with long reasoning before answer)
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Output truncation is response plumbing (control flow), not prompt—deterministic context-keeping requires structural change to post-processing
edits.trigger_condition: Applied after LLM call if ANSWER: line is present; keeps lines from 1 before ANSWER to end; if no ANSWER: found, returns full output unchanged
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Very long extracted answers with verbose explanations would be truncated to answer-adjacent context only; (preservative) passing tasks with concise outputs unaffected; (transfer) preamble truncation generalizes to any task where model over-explains before ANSWER: line
edits.regression_risk: Low—truncation keeps 1 line before ANSWER for immediate context; grader only reads ANSWER: line anyway, so answer content is preserved.
edits.mechanism: Simplify output by keeping only lines from 1 line before ANSWER: to end, discarding verbose preamble; since grader extracts only ANSWER: line, this reduces confusion without loss.
